name: Talbot calotype paper-negative photography
description: The calotype developed a latent image in a paper negative, from which multiple positive prints could be made.

impact.note: Developed negatives giving many prints improved existing photography; the process itself saw limited use, but negative-positive practice in later photography descends from it.

links.statement: The calotype and daguerreotype were distinct early photographic processes.
links.scope: Shared family of photographic image-making, not transmission or technical identity.
